Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is a bacterial disease that causes small, dark lesions on tomato leaves and can also affect fruit.
symptoms: Leaf damage that may expand over time
Dark lesions may also appear on fruit
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.recommendation: Inspect affected plants carefully, remove severely affected material where appropriate, and maintain good field sanitation. Avoid working with wet foliage because moisture can encourage bacterial spread.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a fungal disease that commonly produces dark lesions with characteristic concentric ring patterns on older tomato leaves.
symptoms: Lower leaves are often affected first
Tomato___Early_blight.recommendation: Remove severely affected leaves, improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and maintain good sanitation around tomato plants.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is a destructive disease that can rapidly damage tomato foliage and fruit under favorable environmental conditions.
symptoms: Brown or dark areas on stems
Dark lesions may develop on fruit
Tomato___Late_blight.recommendation: Monitor plants closely, remove severely infected material, improve air circulation, and seek locally appropriate disease-management guidance when symptoms are confirmed.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Tomato leaf mold is a fungal disease that primarily affects foliage, especially under humid conditions.
symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces
Olive or grayish growth on leaf undersides
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.recommendation: Improve ventilation, reduce prolonged humidity around foliage, avoid unnecessary leaf wetness, and remove heavily affected plant material.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot produces numerous small circular lesions and commonly begins on lower tomato leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.recommendation: Remove severely affected leaves, maintain sanitation, improve air circulation, and avoid overhead watering where possible.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-Spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny pests that feed on plant tissues and can cause stippling, discoloration, and leaf decline.
symptoms: Fine webbing may be visible in severe infestations
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.recommendation: Inspect leaf undersides for mites and webbing. Monitor populations regularly and use locally appropriate integrated pest-management practices.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Target spot is a fungal disease that can produce circular lesions with patterns resembling concentric targets.
Tomato___Target_Spot.recommendation: Remove severely affected plant material, improve air circulation, reduce prolonged leaf wetness, and maintain good crop sanitation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus can cause severe leaf curling, yellowing, and reduced plant growth.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.recommendation: Inspect plants for symptoms and potential whitefly vectors. Remove severely affected plants where appropriate and use integrated pest-management practices.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus can cause mottled leaf coloration, distorted growth, and reduced plant performance.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.recommendation: Maintain strict sanitation, avoid spreading plant sap between plants, remove infected material where appropriate, and use clean tools and planting material.

Tomato___healthy.recommendation: Continue regular plant monitoring and maintain good agricultural and crop-management practices.
